overview.title: Overview
overview.text: Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga is uniquely situated on an 'Om' shaped island called Mandhata, at the confluence of the Narmada and Kaveri rivers. The Jyotirlinga is considered to be a single entity split into two temples: Omkareshwar on the island and Mamleshwar on the mainland.

mythology.title: Mythological Origin
mythology.text: There are two main legends. One tells of Vindhya Parvat's penance to please Shiva, who appeared here. Another narrates the story of King Mandhata, who performed severe penance, leading Shiva to manifest himself as a Jyotirlinga. At the request of the Devas, the linga split into two, Omkareshwar and Mamleshwar.

architecture.title: Architectural Highlights
points: The Omkareshwar temple is built in the Nagara style of architecture.
The main sanctum has a low roof, and the lingam is always partially submerged in water.
The temple is adorned with intricately carved pillars and a multi-storied shikhara.
The Mamleshwar temple, located on the south bank, is an ancient stone structure with inscriptions dating back centuries.
Pedestrian bridges connect the island to the mainland, offering scenic views of the Narmada.

significance.title: Spiritual Significance
points: The island itself is considered a sacred symbol, shaped like the primordial sound 'Om'.
The Jyotirlinga is technically one but worshipped in two forms, signifying the form and formless aspects of God.
A 'Parikrama' (circumambulation) of the Mandhata island is considered a highly meritorious act.
The Narmada river is one of the holiest rivers in Hinduism, and a dip here is spiritually purifying.

events.event: References to this holy site are found in ancient scriptures.
The region was a prominent center of Shaivism under the Paramara dynasty.
The temple was renovated and patronized by the Holkar queen, Ahilyabai.

items.text: It is believed that Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati visit here daily to play a game of dice (Chaupar).
The natural shape of the island as 'Om' makes the entire landmass sacred.
Adi Shankaracharya is said to have met his guru, Govinda Bhagavatpada, in a cave here.

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Omkareshwar offers a pilgrimage that is deeply intertwined with nature. The sacred island, the holy Narmada, and the dual temples create a unique spiritual ambiance that brings peace and solace to every visitor.

aboutPostCards.title: Major Festivals
items: Maha Shivratri – The biggest festival, celebrated with great enthusiasm.
Narmada Jayanti – The birth of the river Narmada is celebrated with special rituals.
Kartik Purnima – The temple is beautifully decorated and a fair is held.

aboutPostCards.title: Nearby Attractions
items: Siddhanath Temple – A fine example of early medieval Brahminical architecture.
24 Avatars – A group of Hindu and Jain temples.
Kajal Rani Cave – A scenic spot offering panoramic views.
Mamleshwar Temple – The other half of the Jyotirlinga on the mainland.

methods.title: By Road
methods.description: Omkareshwar is easily accessible by road from major cities like Indore, Ujjain, and Khandwa.

methods.title: Nearest Railway
methods.description: Omkareshwar Road Railway Station (12 km) is on a local line. The major nearby station is Indore (77 km).

methods.title: Nearest Airport
methods.description: Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar Airport, Indore (IDR), is approximately 80 km away.
